newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-TROUBLED LENS SUSPEND DOPE CASE RYCHKOV.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TROUBLED LENS SUSPEND DOPE CASE RYCHKOV.

text.p: Troubled French first division Lens on Monday indefinitely suspended their Russian midfielder Sacha Rychkov, who tested positive for cannabis after a recent league match, and axed playmaker Frederic Meyrieu.
The northern club, 16th after leading the table in the first month of the season, also said they have signed 34-year-old former France international Philippe Vercruysse from FC Sion of Switzerland.

The 22-year-old Rychkov, who signed a four-year contract with Lens when he joined them from Standard Liege of Belgium in the off-season, tested positive for cannabis after the match against Strasbourg on November 23, the club said.
Lens president Gervais Martel said: "We have decided to suspend his contract temporarily because in 99 percent of cases the counter test confirms the use of drugs."
The French Football Federation, awaiting the result of the test on the player's second urine sample, has not yet ruled on the case.
Meyrieu has been dropped from the first team squad "for his insufficient performance on the pitch", Martel told a news conference.

Lens, eliminated by Lazio of Italy in the first round of the UEFA Cup, quickly fell from the top of the table and have picked up only one point from their last eight league matches. They are only three points clear of the four-team relegation zone.
